category_title: Low-achieving students who identify a lack of depth and thought-provoking questions in their inquiry
minimal_context: The student is evaluating their individual contributions to the Knowledge Forum using the Knowledge Connections Analyzer tool.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please open the Knowledge Connections Analyzer tool and use your task sheet to evaluate your individual contributions to the Knowledge Forum.

STUDENT: Okay, I am looking at it. I am just noticing the quantitative data generated by the KCA right now, like how many times things were clicked.

TUTOR: What do those numbers tell you about your notes?

STUDENT: According to the KCA data, my notes have been read a lot, but built on less. What is worse, no notes are referred to by others.

TUTOR: How do you feel about that result?

STUDENT: I am not happy with the quality of my notes; it has much room to be improved. I am wondering whether my notes have been improved and the ideas have been developed. My notes lack thought-provoking questions, but I am only seeing these numbers and I'm not sure how to use this to actually fix the problem.

options.A: Allow the student to keep their KCA task sheet under the condition that they do not show it to their group members, and break off for a scheduled lunch.
options.B: Ignore negative behavior during the KCA analysis, including motor ones (getting out of seat, standing up, moving chairs) and verbal ones (talking to a peer, speaking out of turn).
options.C: Provide direct explanations of the meaning of the KCA output and explicitly scaffold the community orientation intended with 'Are we a community that collaborates?' into focus for the student.
options.D: Allow the student to work at their own pace on the KCA task sheet and take a break from the Knowledge Forum as and when they want during the session.
